title: Window cleaning from the ground and with extension equipment
audience: Trained cleaners who clean internal and external glazing that can be reached from the ground or with extension equipment, in any cleaning-group business. Work that needs a ladder, platform, rope or other height access is outside this lesson's method and is governed by the stop-work rule and the licence notice.
learningOutcomes: Set up a window-cleaning area with barriers and warning signs before any glass is wet.
Wear the gloves and eye protection required for window work, and explain why each is needed.
Apply a diluted cleaning solution with a ferret or dolly, allow contact time, and remove it with overlapping figure-of-eight passes.
Use extension equipment for glazing that cannot be reached from the ground, and apply the stop-work rule when it cannot be reached safely.
Inspect finished glass, frames and ledges for smears, runs and standing water, and correct them.
Wash, dry, colour-code and store window equipment so that clean and dirty equipment never mix.

instruction.heading: Scope of this lesson and what it does not grant
instruction.body: This lesson teaches the ground-level method for internal and external glazing, and the method for glazing you can reach safely with extension equipment. The scope of work for each site decides which glazing is included. Where the work includes internal and external glass, the cleaner cleans both in line with the site's scope. Work that needs a ladder, a platform, a rope or any other form of height access is not covered by this method, and the lesson does not give you the authority or the training to do it. Completing this lesson does not make you licensed or authorised for height work of any kind.

instruction.heading: Protective clothing and equipment
instruction.body: Gloves and goggles are worn for window cleaning every time. Glass cleaning solutions, dust and bacteria on frames and sills can reach the skin and the eyes during wiping and during the rinse, so both must be covered. Before you start, check and wash every piece of equipment: buckets, cloths, ferrets, blades and extension poles. Wash them so that two products are never mixed by accident, because mixed chemicals can give off fumes that could be breathed in. Well-kept equipment lasts longer, and it gives the customer a better result. Confirm each chemical has its manufacturer's label displayed and that you know its dilution before you open it.

instruction.heading: Access, barriers and ventilation
instruction.body: Before you wet any glass, set out a barrier around the area where you are working, and display warning signs where people will see them. The barrier stops pedestrians and customers from walking under or through the work. Open windows or doors where possible, so that you and your colleagues are not standing in fumes. For glazing you cannot reach from the ground, use the extension pole instead of stepping onto furniture, boxes or a ladder. If the extension pole cannot reach the glass safely, the stop-work rule in this lesson applies.

instruction.heading: Applying, removing and checking the solution
instruction.body: Apply the diluted solution to the glass with a ferret or a dolly, so that the whole pane is wet. Leave the solution for its contact time, so that it can loosen the dirt; do not scrub the glass dry while it is working. Remove the solution with overlapping figure-of-eight passes, starting at the top corner of the pane. Wipe the blade on a clean part of the cloth after each pass, because a dirty blade is the most common cause of smears. Wipe the window frames and ledges to remove any water that has run off the glass. Then check the pane for runs and smears in good light, and correct any faults before you move to the next pane.

instruction.heading: Height and ladder work: the stop-work rule
instruction.body: You must stop work and report to your supervisor, and must not climb or place a ladder, when any of the following applies: the glass cannot be reached from the ground or with the supplied extension equipment; you would need to stand on furniture, a box, a step or a ladder; the surface you would stand on is not stable or is wet; you cannot see the work area clearly; there are overhead power lines or other hazards near the work area that you have not been trained to manage; or you are unsure whether the work is covered by your training. Stopping is the correct action, and it is not a failure. The supervisor decides how the glazing is cleaned, and by whom.

instruction.heading: Licence notice: working at height
instruction.body: Working at height, including on ladders, platforms and rope-access systems, may require a specific training qualification or a licence in the state or territory where the work is done. This lesson does not grant a licence, a certificate or any authority to do height work. A worker who has completed this lesson must not carry out height work unless the required training or licence is held and the work is authorised.

instruction.heading: Storage and colour coding
instruction.body: Buckets, cloths, ferrets and blades must be washed thoroughly after use. Stand buckets upside down so they air dry, and hang the cloths and ferrets over the top. Store window equipment in colours that are kept for window work, for example all red cloths together and all blue buckets together. Keep clean equipment and dirty equipment apart, so that a dirty cloth never touches a clean area. Colour coding also keeps unpleasant odours and germs away from the customer.

procedure: Read the scope of work and the site notes, and identify which glazing is included. For any pane you cannot reach from the ground or with the supplied extension equipment, apply the stop-work rule and report it.
Check and wash the buckets, cloths, ferrets, blades and extension poles. Confirm that no two products are being mixed, and that each chemical has its label displayed.
Put on gloves and goggles before you handle any solution or wet glass.
Set out the barrier and display warning signs around the work area. Open windows or doors where possible to ventilate.
Dilute the cleaning solution to the manufacturer's directions and apply it to the glass with a ferret or dolly, so the whole pane is wet.
For glazing out of ordinary reach, use the extension pole. Do not stand on furniture, boxes, steps or ladders.
Allow the solution its contact time so that it loosens the dirt. Do not scrub the glass dry during this time.
Remove the solution with overlapping figure-of-eight passes, starting from the top corner of the pane.
After each pass, wipe the excess water off the blade on a clean part of the cloth.
Wipe the window frames and ledges to remove water that has run off the glass.
Check the pane for runs and smears in good light. Correct any fault before you move to the next pane.
Wash, dry and hang the cloths and ferrets. Stand the buckets upside down to air dry. Clean the blades.
Store the window equipment with its colour group, keeping clean and dirty equipment apart. Store chemicals with the spray switched off.
Remove the barrier and warning signs once the area is dry and safe, and check that no water is left on the floor where people will walk.

workedExamples.situation: A first-floor window is above the reach of your extension pole, and the only way to reach it would be to stand on a plastic chair.
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop. Do not stand on the chair or any other unstable item. The glass is outside the ground-level method, so you report it to your supervisor. The supervisor decides how it is cleaned, and by whom, and whether the required training or licence applies. Leave the barrier in place until the supervisor has decided.

workedExamples.situation: After you have finished a pane, you see a line of streaks across the glass, and the pane is in direct sun.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the most likely cause, and what do you do next?
workedExamples.reasoning: A dirty blade or a missed wipe after a pass is the most likely cause. Wipe the blade clean, wipe the frame and ledge, and then go over the streaked area with overlapping figure-of-eight passes. Check again in good light. If the glass is in direct sun, work on a shaded pane first, because the solution can dry before it is removed.

workedExamples.situation: Your bucket and the cloth you pick up have been used for a bathroom floor yesterday, and the cloth is the same colour as the one for windows.
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Wash the bucket and cloth thoroughly and check the colour group. A cloth or bucket used on washroom or floor work must not be used on glass, and a cloth that is not clean must not be used on glass at all. Set the equipment aside for washing and use a clean set for the window.

equipmentAndPpe: Gloves for handling solutions and wet glass.
Buckets, cloths, ferrets or dollies, and blades, all colour-coded for window work.
Extension poles for glazing out of ordinary reach.
Approved window-cleaning solution, with its manufacturer's label and safety data sheet available.
Barrier and warning signs for the work area.

commonErrors.error: Using a dirty blade or cloth, which leaves smears and streaks on the glass.
commonErrors.prevention: Wipe the blade after every pass and change to a clean part of the cloth when it is wet.

commonErrors.error: Standing on furniture or a ladder to reach a window that the extension pole cannot reach.
commonErrors.prevention: Apply the stop-work rule, report the glass to your supervisor, and do not climb.

commonErrors.error: Mixing two chemicals in the same bucket, or reusing a bucket that held a different product.
commonErrors.prevention: Wash and check every bucket before use, and use one product at its label dilution.

commonErrors.error: Leaving the barrier off, so that people walk through the wet area or under the work.
commonErrors.prevention: Set out the barrier and signs before any glass is wet, and keep them up until the area is dry.

commonErrors.error: Letting the solution dry on the glass during the contact time, which leaves marks.
commonErrors.prevention: Work in shade where possible, and remove the solution before it dries.

commonErrors.error: Storing a wet or dirty cloth with the clean set, which spreads dirt to the next job.
commonErrors.prevention: Wash, dry and hang each cloth in its colour group, and keep dirty equipment separate.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Working at height, including ladders, platforms and rope-access systems, may require specific training or a licence in the state or territory where the work is done. This lesson does not grant any licence, certificate or authority for height work.

Stop-work rule (team rule, not a legal statement): stop and report when the glass cannot be reached safely from the ground or with extension equipment, when you would need to stand on furniture, a box, a step or a ladder, when the surface is unstable or wet, when overhead power lines or other hazards are near, or when you are unsure whether the task is covered by your training.
Chemical use follows the label and the safety data sheet for the product. Dilution, contact time and protective equipment are set by the manufacturer. Do not mix products.
Ventilation: open windows or doors where possible so that no one nearby breathes fumes. Keep customers and bystanders away from the work area.
Slips and falls: wet glass, wet frames and wet floors are slip hazards. Keep warning signs up until the floor is confirmed dry.

qualityStandard: Barrier and warning signs in place before any glass is wet.
Gloves and goggles worn for the whole task.
Each pane is free of smears and runs when checked in good light.
Frames and ledges are wiped and free of standing water.
No height work carried out, and every pane that could not be reached safely is recorded and reported.
Equipment washed, dried, colour-coded and stored with clean and dirty equipment kept apart.
documentationEvidence: Scope check record: which glazing was cleaned, and which panes were reported under the stop-work rule.
Chemical record: product name, dilution used and the batch or lot if your business records it.
Defect or re-clean record for any pane that needed more than one pass.
Incident or near-miss record for any height or ladder situation, and the supervisor's decision.
Equipment wash and colour-group check record.
summary: Set the barrier and signs first, and wear gloves and goggles for the whole task.
Use one approved product at its label dilution, and remove it with overlapping figure-of-eight passes.
Wipe the blade after every pass, and check each pane in good light.
Stop and report any glass you cannot reach safely. Do not climb. Height work is outside this lesson and needs the required training or licence, which this lesson does not grant.
Wash, dry and colour-code the equipment, and keep clean and dirty equipment apart.

knowledgeChecks.question: Before you wet any glass, what must be in place first?
options: The barrier and warning signs for the work area
A chair placed under the window to reach the top
The cloths already hung up to dry on the line

knowledgeChecks.question: A window is out of reach from the ground, and the only way to reach it is a ladder. What do you do?
options: Use a sturdy chair on a level floor and be careful and keep your weight low
Stop, do not climb, and report it so the supervisor decides how it is handled
Clean the lower half only, and leave the upper half for later in the day

knowledgeChecks.question: Which method removes the cleaning solution and leaves the glass smear-free?
options: Circular scrubbing, letting the solution dry on the glass
One straight pass from top to bottom, then move on
Overlapping figure-of-eight passes, wiping the blade after each pass
